newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Waste agrees with regulators.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Waste agrees with regulators.

text.p: Canada's Competition Bureau said on Wednesday it has reached an agreement with Canadian Waste Services Inc, a subsidiary of USA Waste Services Inc, dealing with the company's purchase of the Canadian solid waste assets of Allied Waste Industries Inc.

The bureau found that the purchase would substantially reduce or even prevent competition in four Canadian markets, Raymond Pierce, assistant deputy director for the mergers branch of the competition bureau, said in a phone interview.
But the bureau was able to reach an agreement with Canadian Waste without taking measures against the company, he said.
The company and the bureau need to have their agreement approved by Canada's Competition Tribunal before it takes effect, Pierce said. That process could take several weeks.
The compromise involves Canadian Waste selling the assets it bought from Allied Waste in Sarnia, Ontario. In Brantford, Ontario, Canadian Waste has agreed to sell its own operations.
In Ottawa and the nearby Outaouais area in Quebec, Canadian Waste has agreed not to take control of the Allied assets.
Canadian Waste bought the assets of Allied Waste Holdings (Canada) Ltd in January. Allied earlier bought the solid waste business of Laidlaw Inc in December 1996.
"The major point from our perspective is we think this is good for the residents," Pierce said. "We think consumers will directly benefit from increased competition."
